Four reasons boards choose Sussex on price

Clear pricing and a team that does the work, so your board knows what it is paying for before the project starts.

1

No percentage project fees

Project compensation is agreed with your board in advance. There is no fee for simply collecting bids and issuing notices.

2

In-house trades, at cost

Carpenters, plumbers, electricians and painters on our own payroll. Labour and materials are billed at cost, with no markup.

3

Contractor pricing

Preferential rates built on more than 45 years of volume work.

4

No admin add-ons

Printing and couriers only, and those go away when owners go paperless.

What you will not pay with Sussex

Costs boards often get surprised by

  • Percentage-based project fees
  • Markup on in-house labour or materials
  • A fee for collecting bids and issuing notices
  • Admin add-ons beyond printing and couriers

Switching management companies

A change of manager can be planned and calm. Here is what to look for, and how we handle the handover.

What boards tell us before they switch

Slow answers

Messages to the manager sit for days, and directors end up chasing for updates.

Hard-to-read financials

Statements arrive late or without the context a board needs to decide.

Repairs that stall

Quotes, contractors and follow-ups drift with no clear owner.

A revolving door

The manager changes often, and the building's history walks out the door.

How it works

A transition in five steps

Talk it through

[A confidential call with a director. No obligation.]

We read your agreement

[We review notice and termination terms with the board.]

You get a written proposal

[Scope, fees and a named manager.]

We plan the handover

[Records, bank signing, contractors, vendor contracts.]

Owners are informed

[Clear notice of new contacts and payment details.]
